cells.tense: Here, with the pen, what you picture and what you practise feed each other.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Next time you sit down to practise, start with the part that's already pulling you, and let that pull decide where the work begins. No forcing a direction from the top.
cells.core:
What you picture and what you practise are in the same room now. The images aren't floating above the repetitions; they come up out of them, carrying weight from what you have lived through. The work moves in small steps toward something you can name, and it holds steady because you walk toward it instead of lunging. The session has somewhere it's going, and the somewhere is yours.

When the practice stalls, don't reach for a bigger plan. Let the pull pick the starting point, and take a first step from there. Forcing clarity will look like discipline, but the path that reveals itself comes from what you actually want. Begin where the feeling is, and the next piece shows up on its own.
cells.sheetLine: Your practice is where the images land and get shaped.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity — trusting the next step to show itself
cells.place: the small steady practice kept lit by attention, alone, session by session

cells.tense: Tomorrow's bright vision has replaced today's session, and the dream feels more solid than the work under your hands.
cells.act: make room for it without steering it
cells.ask: Give one session this week its full time, then leave it alone. No deciding what it should become, no forcing a result out of it.
cells.core:
You rehearse the outcome until the outcome is more solid than the next repetition. The dream already has a shape, a whole future built on top of a practice that hasn't fully happened. The pictures are rich; they've started standing in for the work instead of pointing at it. The rehearsing happens in the chair about as often as the session does.

This week, give the practice room and ask nothing of it. It's young enough to want tending, not steering. Let the plan be smaller than the vision, keep the session short, and don't decide what it's for. A thing left alone grows differently from a thing pushed. The hands need to touch the work that's here, not the version ahead of it.
cells.sheetLine: The dream has outgrown the practice that made it.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity — trusting the next step to show itself

cells.tense: You have been standing at the same door a while, unwilling to step into the uncertain part again.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: Sit down to practise without a plan, and take the first thing that shows up as worth your attention. Where the session goes after that can come later.
cells.core:
The practice still happens, but the meaning has gone flat. You do the repetitions because they're on the list, not because anything under them is asking for attention. Trust in not-knowing has turned into distrust; if it can't be measured or scheduled, it doesn't count. The symbolic gets cut off, intuition gets overruled, and the whole thing grows smaller while the sessions continue.

Before the next session, let your own sense of which piece matters arrive first. Knowing what to attend to comes before the reasons do. Not the full schedule — the part that plainly matters, and the rest left where it is. Begin there, and the practice finds its depth again.
cells.sheetLine: The practice continues while its meaning has gone quiet.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity — trusting the next step to show itself
cells.place: the small steady practice kept lit by attention, alone, session by session

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are still writing in, and the dream goes on without your name on it.
cells.act: keep the steady light lit by attention, not flash
cells.ask: Take the plainest version of your practice and do that, unhurried. Let the steady version be enough this time, and see what it does while it runs.
cells.core:
You keep the practices going, you refine them, you show up — and the guidance inside them doesn't get called your vision. The sessions do their work, shaping what you notice and what you reach for, but the shaping stays out of view. You'd say you're just practising. Meanwhile something under the repetitions has been choosing what matters, and it's been doing that quietly.

Go back to the plain version first. Keep the light lit by attention rather than by flash. What flows out of practice shows up in what you choose next, and choosing it deliberately is the whole of the work here. Start with one plain session and let the rest follow from it.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is yours and its guidance has gone unnamed.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity — trusting the next step to show itself
cells.place: the small steady practice kept lit by attention, alone, session by session
